title: Router middleware, error handling, request ids and API-key auth
body:
The router can't do cross-cutting concerns. Refactor `src/router.js` and wire it into the app:

1. `router.use(fn)` registers middleware `async (ctx, next) => response`. Middleware run in registration order before the matched handler; `return next()` continues the chain; returning a response without calling `next` short-circuits.
2. `router.dispatch(ctx)` runs middleware + the matched route and returns the response. `ctx` is `{ method, path, params, query, headers, body, state: {} }` (dispatch fills `params` and a fresh `state` if missing). When no route matches → `{ status: 404, body: { error: 'Not found' } }` (middleware still run first).
3. Errors thrown by middleware or handlers: if the error has a numeric `status`, respond `{ status: err.status, body: { error: err.message } }`; otherwise `{ status: 500, body: { error: 'Internal error' } }` — never leak the original message.
4. In `createApp`:
   - the handler accepts `req.headers` (default `{}`) and passes them in ctx;
   - a middleware adds a unique `x-request-id` header to **every** response (merge into `response.headers`);
   - API-key auth: when `process.env.API_KEYS` (comma-separated, whitespace-tolerant; read on every request) is set, `POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE` requests need a matching `x-api-key` header, else `401 { error }`. `GET` never needs a key. When `API_KEYS` is unset, auth is off.
5. Keep all existing routes working. Add tests.
plan:
Refactor Router to support middleware registration (use) and dispatching (dispatch) with error handling; wire middleware into createApp to add request ids and API key auth; update server handler to use router.dispatch and propagate headers into ctx. Add tests for request id and API-key auth while keeping existing routes working.
1. Refactor src/router.js to add middleware support and dispatch with error handling
2. Update src/server.js to pass headers into ctx, register middlewares (request id and API-key auth), and use router.dispatch in handler
3. Update test/server.test.js: add tests for x-request-id header and API key auth, keep existing tests intact
requirements: Add Router.use(fn) that registers middleware functions to run in registration order before handlers. Middleware signature: async (ctx, next) => response or await next().

Add Router.dispatch(ctx) which fills ctx.params and ctx.state (if missing) and runs middleware chain followed by the matched route handler, returning a response object { status, body, headers? }. If no route matches return { status: 404, body: { error: 'Not found' } } (after running middleware).

Middleware and handlers errors must be caught by dispatch: if thrown error has numeric status -> response { status: err.status, body: { error: err.message } }, otherwise -> { status: 500, body: { error: 'Internal error' } } (do not leak original message).
createApp's handler must accept req.headers (default {}) and pass them into ctx.headers when calling router.dispatch.
Add a middleware that ensures every response contains an x-request-id header — generate a unique id for every request, and merge into response.headers. The header must be present on all responses.

Implement API-key auth as middleware: when process.env.API_KEYS is set (comma-separated values; trim whitespace and re-read per request), for methods POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE require matching x-api-key header; if missing or invalid respond 401 with body { error: 'Unauthorized' } (or equivalent error message). GET requests never require a key. When API_KEYS is unset, auth is disabled.
Keep all existing routes working (health, books, books/:id, cart/quote) and existing behaviors (404 for not found book, etc).

Add tests: cover that x-request-id is added to responses; when API_KEYS is set, POST /cart/quote requires a valid x-api-key header and unauthorized requests receive 401; existing server tests continue to pass.
Do not leak internal error messages for non-status errors; status-bearing errors should be reflected in response status and message.
Update code so router.match is still used internally or compatible; ensure no other modules require signature changes beyond createApp using headers and router.dispatch.
Read process.env.API_KEYS on every request (do not cache across requests).
summary:
Implemented middleware support in Router and wired into createApp. Changes:
- src/router.js: added middlewares array, use(fn) and async dispatch(ctx) which runs middleware chain then matched handler, fills ctx.params/state, and captures errors producing sanitized responses.
- src/server.js: registered two middlewares on router: one adds x-request-id header to every response (generates id per request), another enforces API key auth when process.env.API_KEYS is set (reads env per request, supports comma-separated keys, protects POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE). Updated handler to build ctx including headers and call router.dispatch.
- test/server.test.js: added tests verifying x-request-id is present and API key protection behavior (sets/restores process.env.API_KEYS).

Verification: Ran npm test. All tests related to this change pass. There is one pre-existing failing test (math divide by zero) noted but unchanged.

After review: Implemented middleware-capable Router and integrated into createApp. Changes:
- src/router.js: added middlewares array, use(fn) and dispatch(ctx). Dispatch fills ctx.params/state, runs middleware chain then handler, returns responses, and sanitizes errors (status-bearing errors reflected; other errors return 500). If ctx.state.requestId is set, dispatch ensures error responses include x-request-id header.
- src/server.js: createApp now registers two middlewares: request-id (generates per-request id, stores in ctx.state.requestId, and ensures x-request-id merged into any downstream response via finally; dispatch also attaches id on thrown errors), and API-key auth (reads process.env.API_KEYS per request, trims keys, enforces for POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE using x-api-key header). Handler now builds ctx including headers and calls router.dispatch.
- test/server.test.js: added tests for x-request-id header presence and API key auth behavior; preserved existing server tests.

Verified by running npm test --silent. All tests related to these changes pass. One unrelated pre-existing failing test (math divide by zero) remains unchanged.
